title: Counting the Rework Courtesy Allowance by Source Service (Workmanship Warranties)
content:
**Counting rule.** Under the Workmanship Warranties, the rework courtesy allowance on a covered network rework, being the plan's courtesy rental days as counted into the rework courtesy rental days, is counted according to the customer-pay service the coverage was issued on, held under Customer-Pay Repairs:

| Customer-Pay Repairs service the coverage was issued on | How the rework courtesy allowance is counted |
|---|---|
| Customer-Pay Collision Service or Complete Refinish Service | the plan's courtesy rental days are treated as business days and converted to calendar days by multiplying them by the business-to-calendar ratio of 1.4 and rounding up to a whole day |
| Panel Repair Service or Bumper Refinish Service | the plan's courtesy rental days plus the handover days, 1 day |
| any other source work | the plan's courtesy rental days counted one for one |

## Worked figures (hypothetical plan courtesy rental days)

| Plan's courtesy rental days | Collision or Complete Refinish source | Panel or Bumper Refinish source | Other source work |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 3 multiplied by 1.4 is 4.2, rounded up: 5 days | 3 plus 1: 4 days | 3 days |
| 5 | 5 multiplied by 1.4 is 7.0, already whole: 7 days | 5 plus 1: 6 days | 5 days |
| 0 | 0 days | 0 plus 1: 1 day | 0 days |

## Points of judgement

- Rounding is upward, to the next whole day, and applies only to the converted figure of a Customer-Pay Collision Service or Complete Refinish Service source.
- A coverage issued on an insurance claim repair is "any other source work": its plan's courtesy rental days count one for one.
